facts.statement: In frog embryos, Meis proteins help organize the development of the hindbrain and neural crest.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Proteins related to Meis are found in simple animals such as jellyfish and flatworms, as well as in single-celled organisms.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The study aimed to find out when Meis proteins gained the ability to trigger the formation of neural structures during the history of animal life.
facts.subject: other

facts.statement: Experiments in frogs showed that specific parts of the Meis protein are enough to start spinal cord development but are not enough to start hindbrain development.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: A specific region at the end of Meis proteins is responsible for triggering hindbrain development.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Versions of the Meis protein found in the simple animal Trichoplax and in algae have a core structural part but are missing a region found in more complex animals.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Surprisingly, the ancient versions of the protein from algae and Trichoplax were able to trigger hindbrain and neural crest development in frogs, even though they lack the part that modern animal versions need.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The findings suggest that early versions of these proteins had the built-in ability to create complex vertebrate brain structures before those structures actually evolved.
